question: The archaeological site of Inamgaon is situated at the bank of river Ghod which is a tributary of __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhima**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The river Ghod is a tributary of the Bhima River which is a major river in Maharashtra, India.
 
• Inamgaon, an archaeological site located on the banks of the river Ghod, has been studied extensively for its ancient human settlements.
 
• The Bhima River itself is a major tributary of the Krishna River, which is one of the longest rivers in India.
 
• The Bhima River basin is important for its agricultural and cultural significance in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inamgaon Archaeological Site**

 
 
• Inamgaon is an archaeological site located in the Pune district of Maharashtra.
 
• The site has revealed substantial evidence of Chalcolithic (Copper Age) human settlements.
 
• Excavations at Inamgaon have uncovered artifacts like pottery, tools, and remnants of ancient dwellings.
 
• The site provides valuable insights into the lifestyle, culture, and agricultural practices of ancient communities.
 
 
 
• **Bhima River**
 
 
• The Bhima River originates from Bhimashankar hills in the Western Ghats, Maharashtra.
 
• It flows southeast for about 861 kilometers before merging with the Krishna River.
 
• The river passes through several important towns and cities, including Pune and Solapur.
 
• The Bhima River basin is a crucial area for agriculture, supporting crops like sugarcane, millet, and rice.
 
 
 
• **Krishna River**
 
 
• The Krishna River is one of the major rivers in India, originating from Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats.
 
• It flows across the Indian states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The river spans a length of about 1,400 kilometers, making it one of the longest rivers in India.
 
• The Krishna River basin is known for its fertile lands and diverse ecosystems, supporting a wide range of agricultural activities.
